> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cf6bb70e2d98a8502077ccd602b036f0d9086786` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ebcae7d6ca57c11e866bd203e54681f5b86ee011` — the merge of head `d4dc6f350cc47bf56f7f51163ffc59f446c1f614` into base `cf6bb70e2d98a8502077ccd602b036f0d9086786`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ebcae7d6ca57c11e866bd203e54681f5b86ee011 && git checkout ebcae7d6ca57c11e866bd203e54681f5b86ee011
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cf6bb70e2d98a8502077ccd602b036f0d9086786 d4dc6f350cc47bf56f7f51163ffc59f446c1f614 && git checkout -B drift-repro cf6bb70e2d98a8502077ccd602b036f0d9086786 && git merge --no-ff d4dc6f350cc47bf56f7f51163ffc59f446c1f614

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cf6bb70e2d98a8502077ccd602b036f0d9086786
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cf6bb70e2d98a8502077ccd602b036f0d9086786` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bf6fa3de2066ea804f72007c9b9c441e56bd60cc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/presented-invitation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-mailbox-proof.ts, packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/ssoCallbackRefusal.ts, and the pinned vendor at 1.7.12, read from the package store because node_modules is not installed where this review ran (better-auth dist: oauth2/link-account.mjs, oauth2/callback.mjs, db/internal-adapter.mjs, utils/validate-user-info.mjs, api/routes/callback.mjs, api/routes/sign-in.mjs, plugins/generic-oauth, plugins/one-tap, plugins/oauth-proxy; @better-auth/core dist/social-providers; @better-auth/sso dist)
Security-touching: yes

### ① Derived judgments

Judged on the net diff against `main` (7 files, +371 −15). The changeset and the two `content/docs` pages are prose faces, read here for ② only.

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each against the ruling:

- **Narrowed, right: `email_domain`.** A self-serve creation whose vendor method is `oauth` and whose provider did not report the address verified is refused `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`, whatever the deployment declares for email verification: for an address on the allowlist, and for one off it that a pending invitation is addressed to. This is the ruling's first pin and its invitation pin. The PR decides the invitation case **takes the same refusal** and states it in the body, the changeset, both doc pages and the module doc. It is pinned on the real engine: the invitation stays pending, and the provider-verified retry is admitted and accepts the invited role.
- **Narrowed, right: `open` while email verification is in force** (declared absent or `true`), invited or not. The ruling's second pin. "In force" is `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement` over the same `config.emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification` that the better-auth wiring and `getPublicConfig` read, so the gate cannot disagree with the wired or the advertised value. Absent resolves to in force.
- **Unchanged, right (the ruling's controls).**
  - A provider-verified social creation admits, is granted and binds under both postures.
  - The `provider` class (`oauth` with an `oidcProviders` providerId, `sso-oidc`, `sso-saml`) and the `operator` class return before the rule.
  - The first account of a fresh install returns before it, in the same order as under `invite_only`.
  - `open` with the deployment's verification declared off, `invite_only`, and every other self-serve method read as before.
  - `link-account` and `sign-in` are not judged: the rule is about a creation, as the ruling words it.
- **One refusal changes its code, right as an ordering.** Under `email_domain`, an address off the allowlist with no invitation, unverified by the provider, is refused before and after, but the code moves from `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` to `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` because the rule sits ahead of the posture switch. The PR body says so; the changeset's sentence covers the case without naming the moved code.
- **Only the boolean `true` counts as verified**, which is the reading `invitationProofFor` already takes. Fail closed.

Public surface: no wire code, config key, schema or export is added or removed. `audience-posture.ts` is not re-exported from the package entry, so the three optional inputs on `AudienceAdmissionInput` and the two private helpers publish nothing, and the error-code ledger does not move. One new `errorDescription` sentence rides an existing code.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` is correct.

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing: …)` reads `no` with the `narrowing` arm, on the PR body and in the changeset. Nothing widens.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is truthful: no authorable key, accepted value or default moves. The published `AudienceConfigSchema` already says `email_domain` forces email verification on with no opt-out, and `open` forces it on unless the deployment declares it off.
- A non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner. The `!`, **BREAKING**, "What to do" and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are all present.
- The changeset's statements match the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question: keep `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` (A), or a dedicated code (B).**
  - **A stands for this head.** The ruling's words are "refused at the admission gate, as `invite_only` already does", and `invite_only` answers this creation with that code. The code is registered, nothing is added to the surface, and the server's description names the provider-side remedy.
  - **B is escalated to the maintainer.** A new wire code is a ledger entry in `packages/spec`, a constant and console copy: a contract decision, which `security-findings.md` §6 hands to the maintainer. It is not the reviewer's or the dev's to take.
  - What the maintainer weighs:
    - With A, a client cannot tell this refusal from the `invite_only` one, and the two have different remedies.
    - The ledger line for the code reads "audience posture invite_only: self-registration is closed (no pending invitation for this address)", and the console's callback sentence for it is "Ask your administrator to invite you". Both describe the `invite_only` emitters only. For this refusal an invitation does not open the social door (pinned); it opens the invitation mail's own link, where email sign-up is on.
    - The tree holds one precedent each way: `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED` was split from `PASSWORD_EXPIRED` by ruling so that a client can tell the two apart, and `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` stays one code for two emitters because the console's one sentence is true of both.
  - Reviewer's reading: here the remedies differ and no one sentence is true of both emitters, so B is the better end state. If the maintainer keeps one code, the ledger line and the console sentence need rewording so that they are true of every emitter.
  - Timing: the ruling is cheapest before the release that publishes this refusal. After that release, moving the refusal to a new code is a second wire change.
  - Either way the follow-up lands in `ui/` and `packages/spec`, outside this order's surface, as its own card. This head does not wait on it.
- **Dev flags in the PR body**, each confirmed against the tree:
  - The bootstrap carve-out stays ahead of the rule; pinned at the decision level.
  - `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` has no hunk, so the declined "allow but hold" per-provider requirement is not introduced.
  - Three existing call sites moved to `open` with verification declared off; their assertions are unchanged.
  - `deployment()` boots the self-registration set for `open` as well as `email_domain`.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The decision stays pure and the gate's existing probes are unchanged.
- No governed path and no published schema is in the diff. `settleMembership` has no hunk, so ADR-0093 and the binding rule are untouched.
- **Gate verdicts on this head:** 55 check-runs, all completed: 40 success, 15 skipped, none failed, none still running.
  - Success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (10 of 10 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards.
  - Skipped on this pull-request run, among the required contexts: `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI`. The dogfood shards are skipped too; the queue run carries them.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The narrowing against the published spec on `main` takes no declared capability away. `AudienceConfigSchema` declares verification forced on under these postures; the gate now holds a social creation to that at the one admission seam, before anything is written.

- **`audience-posture.ts` holds.** One predicate sits after the class exemptions, the bootstrap carve-out and the vocabulary guard, and before the invitation carve-out and the posture switch, so every admit below it is covered. The module doc, the input docs and the function doc agree with the code sentence by sentence. Tried against the cited code, and held:
  - *A social creation under another method.* In the pinned vendor every social door hands the gate `method: 'oauth'`, which is also the vendor's default; SSO hands `sso-oidc` or `sso-saml`.
  - *`emailVerified` from the caller.* It is `internalAdapter.createUser`'s own input, set by the vendor from the provider adapter. The request body does not reach it.
  - *Providers added later.* Any `socialProviders` key arrives as `oauth` with a providerId outside `oidcProviders` and meets the rule unnamed. Pinned with an unknown providerId and with an absent `emailVerified`.
  - *Operator-registered providers.* `oidcProviders` entries also arrive as `oauth`; `enterpriseOAuthProviderIds()` classes them `provider`, ahead of the rule. Pinned at the decision and at the manager's gate.
  - *`open` with nothing declared.* Resolves to in force. Pinned.
- **`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts` holds.** Three reads are handed to the pure decision: the vendor's `source.method`, `user.emailVerified`, and the live `emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification` through the `config` getter. A refusal returns before anything is staged.
- **`audience-posture.test.ts` holds.** Two top-level describes in the existing harness file: the decision matrix, with a control for each exemption, and the real manager's gate.
- **`invitation-acceptance-verified-address.test.ts` holds.** Real engine, real `sign-in/social` door. The three ruled refusals each assert status, code, no session and unchanged `sys_user`, `sys_account`, `sys_session` and `sys_member` counts. The verified controls assert admission and the default-organization membership. The one rewritten case is the ruled change of outcome, not a deleted pin.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — `method` is optional on `AudienceAdmissionInput`, and it is the one new input whose absence leaves the rule unevaluated; the other two refuse when absent. There is one call site, and it passes it.
- N2 (nit) — the refusal's only prescription is to verify the address with the provider. Where a provider's adapter never reports an address verified, the person cannot follow it. The changeset names the other doors; the runtime sentence does not.
- N3 (nit) — the refusal is pinned through the id-token door only. The browser callback's `error=SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` redirect, which the changeset and the doc page state, rests on the vendor's callback handing any gate refusal to the error URL: read in the vendor, not pinned here.
- N4 (nit) — the rule is keyed on the vendor method `oauth`. A creation method that a later vendor release adds needs classifying against this rule at the bump.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **How this PR's rule and main's seed-staging step meet in `validateAudienceAdmission`.** Read line by line at this head:
  - The order is: class resolution, the read-only probes, `decideAudienceAdmission`, the refusal return, then the stagings (owner-verified stamp, development-seed mark, invitation admission, self-registration grant).
